title: Pokemon SoulGold (v1.1.4)
sources: The ROM itself (SoulGold 1.1.4, pokeemerald-expansion 1.15 build; its map sections are 16-bit): region map section names (each place resolves to a section with maps) and trainer names, teams and levels (Classic and Hard teams), read on the PC with throwaway tools
GitHub Eemeliri/soulgold: README (features, optional level caps) and release notes
pokemonsoulgold.com: changelog, about page, gift Pokémon guide
soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs): FAQ, walkthrough, starters, legendaries; romhackguides.com (1.1.2)

milestones.name: A starter from Elm's case
milestones.tips: Nine starters: Chikorita, Chespin, Sprigatito; Cyndaquil, Fennekin, Torchic; Totodile, Froakie, Popplio. Gold, a second trainer from New Bark, battles you with a Lv 4 Marill. Cherrygrove gives an Alolan Rattata or a Galarian Zigzagoon.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; pokemonsoulgold.com (changelog, gift Pokémon)

milestones.name: Gym 1: Falkner
milestones.badge_note: Zephyr Badge. Optional level cap after it: 19.
milestones.tips: Flying types: Pidgey, Gligar, Pidgeotto (Lv 11-12). Electric, Ice and Rock moves. Hard mode has its own teams (often a level higher, gyms as double battles).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; GitHub Eemeliri/soulgold README and releases

milestones.name: Team Rocket: Proton in Slowpoke Well
milestones.tips: Proton: Nosepass, Houndour, Porygon (Lv 17-18). Fighting moves; Ground for Nosepass and Houndour.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Gym 2: Bugsy
milestones.badge_note: Hive Badge. Optional level cap after it: 26.
milestones.tips: Bug types: Scyther, Whirlipede, Cutiefly (Lv 19-20). Fire, Flying and Rock moves. Hard mode has its own teams (often a level higher, gyms as double battles).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; GitHub Eemeliri/soulgold README and releases

milestones.name: Rival: first battles
milestones.tips: The rival (Silver in the sources) fights you several times; his early team is Haunter, Pawniard, Pidgeotto and his starter at Lv 20-22 (21-22 on Hard). He also gives the Odd Egg (Bagon, Gible, Feebas, Riolu, Jangmo-o, Hisuian Zorua or Goomy). The rival is stored under the player-named placeholder, so the companion can't look this battle up by name; the levels are the ROM's.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; pokemonsoulgold.com (changelog, gift Pokémon)

milestones.name: Gold on Route 34
milestones.tips: Gold again: Zorua, Oricorio, Azumarill (Lv 22).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Gym 3: Whitney
milestones.badge_note: Plain Badge. The Battle Factory opens after this gym.
milestones.tips: Normal types: Audino, Girafarig, Miltank (Lv 25-27). Fighting moves. Her gym opens after the quiz on Radio Tower 1F. Hard mode has its own teams (often a level higher, gyms as double battles).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Gym 4: Morty
milestones.tips: Ghost types: Corsola, Doublade, Misdreavus, Gengar (Lv 33-34). Dark and Ghost moves. After the Burned Tower, Raikou, Entei and Suicune roam. Hard mode has its own teams (often a level higher, gyms as double battles).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; GitHub Eemeliri/soulgold README and releases

milestones.name: Rival: middle battles
milestones.tips: Floatzel or Haunter, Pawniard, Staravia, a Lampent/Weepinbell/Clodsire and his starter's middle stage at Lv 30-33. The rival is stored under the player-named placeholder, so the companion can't look this battle up by name; the levels are the ROM's.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table

milestones.name: Gym: Chuck
milestones.tips: Fighting types: Hitmontop, Mienshao, Poliwrath, Annihilape (Lv 41-42). Psychic, Flying and Fairy moves. Chuck, Jasmine and Pryce scale with your badges: Lv 42 with four, 45 with five, 48 with six.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Eusine
milestones.tips: Golisopod, Wobbuffet, Magnezone (Lv 38-39).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table

milestones.name: Gym: Jasmine
milestones.tips: Steel types: Skarmory, Tinkaton, Magneton, Scizor, Steelix (Lv 44-45) at five badges. Fire, Fighting and Ground moves. Strength comes from the Olivine café.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Gym: Pryce
milestones.badge_note: Glacier Badge. Optional level cap until the Rocket takeover: 55.
milestones.tips: Ice types: Ninetales, Mamoswine, Glaceon, Weavile, Froslass (Lv 47-48) at six badges. Fire, Fighting, Rock and Steel moves.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Rocket hideout in Mahogany
milestones.tips: Petrel (Scrafty, Persian, Pyroar, Weezing (Lv 47-48)) on B3F and Ariana (Arbok, Vileplume, Dragalge (Lv 48-49)) on B2F.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Team Rocket takes the Radio Tower
milestones.tips: Proton on 4F (Crobat, Farigiraf, Porygon-Z, Nidoking, Scrafty (Lv 49-51)), Petrel and Ariana on 5F (Scrafty, Rotom, Persian, Pyroar, Weezing (Lv 48-49); Arbok, Toxapex, Vileplume, Gyarados, Dragalge (Lv 50-51)), Archer at the top (Ninetales, Tauros, Marowak, Slowking, Houndoom (Lv 52-54)). The Mega Ring is yours afterwards, and you choose the Rainbow Wing or the Silver Wing.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Gold in the Ice Path
milestones.tips: Azumarill, Zoroark, Oricorio, Flygon, Ampharos (Lv 54-55). The Ice Path also holds Waterfall.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Gym 8: Clair
milestones.badge_note: Rising Badge: Rock Climb (since 1.1). Optional cap until Ho-Oh or Lugia: 62, then 70 to the Champion.
milestones.tips: Dragons: Altaria, Gyarados, Dragonite, Hydrapple, Kingdra (Lv 57-58). Ice, Dragon and Fairy moves. Hard mode has its own teams (often a level higher, gyms as double battles).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Rival: before the league
milestones.tips: His full team at Lv 48-51 (Gengar or Floatzel, Bisharp, Staraptor and his starter's final stage). The rival is stored under the player-named placeholder, so the companion can't look this battle up by name; the levels are the ROM's.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table

milestones.name: Elite Four: Will
milestones.tips: Farigiraf, Espeon, Slowbro, Reuniclus, Alakazam, Braviary (Lv 66-67). Dark, Ghost and Bug moves.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Koga
milestones.tips: Ariados, Roserade, Muk, Overqwil, Scolipede, Crobat (Lv 67-68). Psychic and Ground moves.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Bruno
milestones.tips: Hitmontop, Heracross, Staraptor, Annihilape, Kommo-o, Machamp (Lv 67-69). Psychic, Flying and Fairy moves.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Karen
milestones.tips: Grimmsnarl, Umbreon, Kingambit, Scrafty, Honchkrow, Absol (Lv 69-70). Fighting, Bug and Fairy moves.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Champion Lance
milestones.tips: Exeggutor, Dragonite, Baxcalibur, Hydrapple, Dragapult, Archaludon (Lv 69-71). Ice and Fairy moves; Archaludon is Steel/Dragon (Fighting, Ground).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Gold on Mt. Silver
milestones.tips: Iron Treads, Zoroark, Baxcalibur, Azumarill, Ampharos, Tangrowth (Lv 73-75).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: League rematch and Title Defense
milestones.tips: The Elite Four return at Lv 85 and Lance at 86; then Title Defense, where the challenger changes (Lv 86 aces include Genesect, Zamazenta and Giratina).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Gym rematches
milestones.tips: The leaders rematch at new places with Lv 76-81 teams, and again with Lv 85 teams holding a legend each.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table

milestones.name: Steven
milestones.tips: Skarmory, Aggron, Cradily, Excadrill, Archeops, Metagross (Lv 80-82); beating him opens Rayquaza at the Embedded Tower.
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table; soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Leaf
milestones.tips: Chansey, Volcarona, Thundurus, Tapu Fini, Dragapult, Venusaur (Lv 85-87).
milestones.source: ROM SoulGold 1.1.4 trainer table

milestones.name: Ho-Oh or Lugia
milestones.tips: After the Radio Tower you pick the Rainbow Wing (Ho-Oh, Tin Tower) or the Silver Wing (Lugia, Whirl Islands); the radio director gives the other after the Elite Four. Legends are boss fights with several HP bars, and a beaten boss is a sure catch.
milestones.source: soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Celebi (Ilex Forest)
milestones.tips: Solve all eight Ruins of Alph puzzles, then see Kurt and visit the Ilex shrine.
milestones.source: soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

milestones.name: Mewtwo (Kitakami Border)
milestones.tips: In the Nameless Dungeon at the Kitakami Border, after the Elite Four (Rock Climb).
milestones.source: soulgold.run (unofficial fan docs)

steps.title: Optional level caps
steps.text: Caps (if turned on): 12, 19, 26, 34, 42, 45, 48, 55 for the Rocket takeover, 58, 62 until Ho-Oh/Lugia, 70 until the Champion.

steps.title: Innate abilities
steps.text: Pokémon gain extra innate abilities at Lv 75, 85 and 95; a bookcase in Elm's lab unlocks them early or turns them off.

steps.title: HMs need the HM and the badge
steps.text: Strength is from the Olivine café, Waterfall from the Ice Path, Rock Climb works after badge 8.

steps.title: Any starter from the casino
steps.text: The Goldenrod casino's gachapon sells starters from every generation (3000+ coins).

steps.title: Dratini in Blackthorn
steps.text: Blackthorn gives a Dratini; answer correctly and it knows Spacial Rend.

secrets.text: Bill gives an Eevee or a Pikachu.
Since 1.1.4 Cursola lives in the waters of Rinto Village.
Regirock in the Vajra Desert: bring a Tyranitar.
Regice on Snowtop Mountain (bring a Baxcalibur); Articuno is up there too (Rock Climb).
Registeel in the Railway Cave: bring a Kommo-o.
Regigigas on Mt. Silver, with all three Regis in the party.
Zapdos on top of the Olivine lighthouse after badge 8.
Primal Dialga at the Spear Pillar.
Most Paradox Pokémon live on Meteor Island; the changed beasts come from the roaming trio.
Shadow Lugia: the Dark Crystal from the abandoned Rocket warehouse south of Route 33.
Latias and Latios in the Vajra temple; the Vajra Pyramid is a battle facility.
The Rocket Arcade pays money; 25 wins give Magearna.
Dream Garden is one of SoulGold's added areas, with Tohjo Pass, Route 50 and Meteor Island.

evolutions.name: Sinistea
evolutions.text: Which tea item you use decides the form it evolves into (1.1).

evolutions.name: Kadabra
evolutions.text: SoulGold's way of evolving trade evolutions is not documented in the sources; in-game trade Pokémon get 12x shiny odds.

notes.title: SoulGold 1.1.4
notes.text: A Johto-only remake on pokeemerald-expansion 1.15 (no Kanto), using an unofficial port of Heart & Soul's assets. 132 areas and every generation's Pokémon, Paradox ones included; Classic and Hard modes. 1.1.4 added innates and night-lighting toggles and an earlier Safari Zone expansion.
notes.source: GitHub Eemeliri/soulgold README and releases; pokemonsoulgold.com (changelog, gift Pokémon)

notes.title: Mega Evolution
notes.text: Every Mega, with type-generic stones (Elm gives your starter's); new Megas for Typhlosion, Meowscarada and Primarina. Press START on the move screen to Mega Evolve.

notes.title: Features
notes.text: DexNav after the first Poké Balls, followers, daily hidden grottoes, a VS Seeker, feather fishing (IV training), a move relearner with a TM tab, Exp. Share before Violet, a Candy Jar after gym 1, shiny odds setting.

notes.title: The beasts
notes.text: Raikou, Entei and Suicune all roam after the Burned Tower; their shininess is rolled when they are released.
